edbDesc: (aka Sedimentation Potential). Potential difference resulting from motion of particles through water, typically due to gravity or centrifugation. The motion disrupts equilibrium symmetry of particle's double layer, viscous flow around the particles drags ions of the diffuse layer from them causing slight displacement between surface charge & electric charge of the diffuse layer, giving the particle a dipole moment, generating electric field.
title: Dorn Effect
pickWhy: Particles settling through water make only a few millivolts; it is a lab measurement, too weak to do a job.
